items.root_cause: test-match-lib's verdict depends on wall-clock load and cannot say which kind of red it is. It runs as a census in test-auditors' early pool while the daily chain is at peak. The 3ca22f fix re-looks blind looks only up to 50 and names only blind looks. Non-blind divergences are counted but never named or re-looked. So a load storm (2,274 blind) always reads as a blind guard. Worse, the 1,641 non-blind divergences are unexplained. The reference is deterministic, so each one is match-lib giving a different answer with no recorded timeout. The engine uses match-lib, so if that is real, a loaded board build could mis-assign products with no could-not-look row. The harness throws away the names that would decide it. Class: every non-blind divergence the harness reports under load (1,641 today, unknown on 09-24 because it was not kept).

root_fix.what: Make the red self-diagnosing. Step 1: name and re-look every divergence, not only blind looks. A still-disagreeing name fails as DRIFT. A non-blind divergence that agrees on re-look fails as a distinct class UNRECORDED (a pure function answered twice differently with no recorded timeout), never as load. Blind looks that resolve on re-look pass as RETRIED (load). Step 2: reproduce under controlled load and find the path that produces UNRECORDED answers.

root_fix.exact_change: (1) test-match-lib.ps1: drop the BlindRetryCap = 50 short-circuit. Re-look every still-blind name AND every row of $diff once in the parent after the pool drains, at the unchanged 250 ms bound (sequential, about 10 ms a name for 4 passes, so about 40 s for today's 3,915). (2) Get-MatchLibVerdict takes the re-look results and prints three counts: DRIFT (disagrees again), UNRECORDED (a non-blind divergence that agreed on re-look) and still-blind. The FAILED line carries the first 15 of DRIFT and UNRECORDED as 'name [path] reference -> fast', each cut to 80 chars, ahead of the blind names. rc stays 1 for any of the three. (3) Write the full lists to one per-run file under $env:TEMP (og-38 naming) and print its path on the FAILED line, so the saved fail copy points at them. (4) Reproduce in a scratch copy of the harness under ops/cpu-load.ps1 (the sanctioned load tool; never hand-rolled burners), with -Workers at the default. Record which path (compiled or powershell-fallback) and which pass produce UNRECORDED rows, and read that path in match-lib.ps1. If a real unrecorded-bound path is found in match-lib.ps1, do NOT fix it in this item: open a money-lane queue item naming the path and the rows (it changes the engine's matcher).
